name: Relevance of LiPP test set (RMSD below 2 Angstrom and PoseBusters valid) to "Choose structural hypotheses to guide experiments"
description: Lipid-protein pose accuracy on complexes released after every tool's training cutoff, as evidence for trusting a predicted ligand complex.

attributes.endpoint: Share of 36 post-cutoff lipid-protein complexes whose predicted lipid pose counts as a success (RMSD below 2 Angstrom and PoseBusters valid)
attributes.rationale: Proxy, not direct: the use case asks whether a predicted interface or complex is reliable enough to guide an experiment, and this protocol answers it for lipid ligands on complexes no tool could have memorised. It does not cover protein-protein interfaces, protein-peptide complexes or drug-like small molecules, and a correct pose does not establish that the interaction matters in the experiment being planned.
constraints: Lipid ligands only; the LiPP authors note that drug-likeness filters exclude most lipids from PDBbind-derived sets.
Compare only within the same criterion and the same dataset column: the full LiPP set includes complexes inside some tools' training windows.
The 36-complex test set is small, so the printed 95% confidence intervals are wide.
Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator before citing a result.
